newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn opposition want vote on Waigel resignation.
newsitem.headline: Bonn opposition want vote on Waigel resignation.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens party are preparing to apply to parliament to vote on whether Finance Minister Theo Waigel should remain in office, a Greens spokeswoman said on Monday.

Waigel has come under fire from the opposition SPD and Greens over his proposal last month to revalue German central bank gold and currency reserves. They accused him of jeopardising the credibility of the Bundesbank.

A spokeswoman for the Greens parliamentary group, Susanne Duewel, told Reuters the two parliamentary groups would also apply for a vote to approve a declaration on Wednesday by the German central bank criticising Waigel's gold plan.
The parliamentary leaders of the Greens, Joschka Fischer, and the SPD, Rudolf Scharping, will reveal the details of their application to parliament at 1000 GMT, she said.
Waigel has repeatedly rejected calls for his resignation and stood by his plan, aimed to help plug budget gaps in a drive to meet criteria for the common European currency.
